(BY SMT V. RAJINI, ADVOCATE)
 THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 05.01.2013 PASSED IN  MVC NO.29/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE,
 MACT, CHALLAKERE, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION  FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF  COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR DICTATING JUDGMENT,
 THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
Nagaraj vs H V Mallikarjuna on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171083369/
1  -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:46093  MFA No. 3957 of 2013  JUDGMENT Disputing the validity of the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Challakere, in MVC No.29/2012 dated 05.01.2013, the present appeal is preferred.
2. This is a claimant's appeal.
The Dispute in the appeal is only with regard to the quantum that is awarded as compensation.
3. The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded compensation of Rs.25,000/- as against the claim of Rs.10,00,000/- and aggrieved thereby the present appeal is preferred.

4. The case of the appellant as borne by record is that on 30.06.2010 while he was proceeding on a motorcycle near Gowripura Gate, one Mahendra Maxi Truck bearing Registration No.KA.16 B.416 approached his motorcycle from the opposite direction driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against his motorcycle.
Due to which he fell down and sustained multiple injuries.
As per the version of the appellant he incurred a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and Rs.25,000/- for food, lodging and other expenses.
It is also his version that as agriculturist he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but due to the injuries sustained he lost his livelihood.

Hence,
he prayed the Tribunal to award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
6. Respondents No.1 and 2 resisted the claim on several grounds, prominent of which are with regard to the expenditure he incurred for the treatment and the nature of injuries sustained.
7. Arguing in respect of merits of the case, learned counsel for the appellant contended that the amount awarded as compensation is meager.
Learned counsel stated that the appellant spent lot of amount towards medical expenses, conveyance and diet.
Learned counsel also states that the appellant suffered with huge pain and suffering and he lost the amenities in life.

Learned counsel also stated that the appellant became totally disabled to work and therefore, the Tribunal NC:
2023:KHC:46093 basing on the evidence produced ought to have awarded the sum claimed as compensation.
8.

When the material available on record is gone through, this Court finds that though the appellant produced Exs.P4, P7 to P17 to establish his version with regard to the treatment that went on and the expenditure incurred, as rightly observed by the Tribunal, the appellant failed to establish the genuineness of those documents.

However, the fact that the appellant sustained a cervical spine Nagaraj vs H V Mallikarjuna on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171083369/
2 injury and composite fracture of right upper end of tibia and fibula which are grievous in nature, is evidenced through the contents of Ex.P4.
A person who sustained such grievous injuries ought to have obtained necessary treatment for recovery.
Also by the nature of injuries sustained, it can be safely presumed that the appellant would not have attended his normal pursuits, at-least for a period of three months.
Having regard to these factors, the amount awarded as compensation by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
9. Taking the nominal income of the appellant as Rs.6,000/- per month by the date of accident, the loss of NC: 2023:KHC:46093 income comes to Rs.18,000/- (6,000x3).

Also having regard to the nature of injuries sustained, an amount of Rs.30,000/- can be awarded under the head pain and suffering and Rs.15,000/- under the head treatment, transportation, extra nourishment, diet and attendant charges.
A nominal amount of Rs.3,000/- can also be awarded under the head loss of amenities in life.

Thus, the compensation which the appellant is entitled to under various heads is as under:
 Sl. Description Amount  No Rs.
 1 Compensation for pain  and suffering for the  grievous injuries 30,000  sustained  2 Expenses which the  appellant would have  incurred for treatment, 15,000  transport, extra  nourishment, diet etc.,
 3 Loss of earnings  18,000  4 Loss of amenities in life  3,000
Total Compensation Rs.66,000  NC: 2023:KHC:46093  10.
Thus, the following  ORDER  (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation awarded by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Challakere, through orders in MVC No.29/2012 dated 05.01.2013 is enhanced from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.66,000/-.

3 (iii) The enhanced amount shall carry the same interest as awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The award of the Tribunal in all other aspects holds good.
